lines.text: Your carpool lost its front seat for 15 mornings to a dupatta nobody's ever seen.
One driver. Three passengers. One front seat.
Week one. Rohan, eight sharp. A dupatta's already there.
Folded. Polite.
Week two. Priya, seven sharp. Dupatta. Plus a steel tiffin.
Week three. Sharma ji, early for once. Dupatta, tiffin, flask of chai.
Still warm.
So they settle it like adults. Coin toss.
Rohan flips. The coin rolls under the car. Into the drain.
Best of three. Two more coins. Same drain.
Then the guard walks over. That's Kapoor aunty's.
Kapoor aunty is not in the carpool.
She rides two stops to the vegetable market.
Arjun thought she was Priya's aunt. Priya thought, Arjun's.
Lesson: if nobody knows who's in your carpool, the dupatta decides.
Fix? A real pool, inside an app. Four names. Then five.
Aunty joined. The roster gave her a driving turn.
Market closed? One tap on skip today, front seat free.
Thursday. Kapoor aunty drives.
The dupatta now reserves the driver's seat.
If a dupatta owns your front seat, try Sahyatri.
